## Pull request overview

Adds a full-featured in-memory driver spec to `@objectstack/spec` and significantly expands the `@objectstack/plugin-driver-memory` implementation to cover more of the driver protocol surface (transactions, projection, strict mode, utilities), along with accompanying tests.

**Changes:**
- Added `MemoryConfigSchema` / `MemoryPersistenceConfigSchema` and a `MemoryDriverSpec` driver definition in spec.
- Enhanced the in-memory driver plugin with initial data loading, strict mode behavior, snapshot-based transactions, field projection, distinct, and store utilities.
- Added/expanded test coverage for both the spec schema and the plugin driver behaviors.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 7 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/spec/src/data/driver/memory.zod.ts | Introduces memory driver config schemas + a driver definition (`MemoryDriverSpec`). |
| packages/spec/src/data/driver/memory.test.ts | Adds schema/spec tests for the new memory driver spec definitions. |
| packages/plugins/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts | Implements new runtime behaviors (transactions, projection, strict mode, etc.) in the plugin driver. |
| packages/plugins/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.test.ts | Expands plugin tests to cover new driver functionality and behaviors. |
| packages/plugins/driver-memory/src/index.ts | Exposes the driver config type and simplifies plugin enable/registration logic. |
</details>

`create()`/`update()` switched `created_at`/`updated_at` to ISO strings, but other code paths in this driver still appear to use `Date` objects (e.g. bulk/updateMany logic). Mixing timestamp representations makes downstream code brittle. Consider standardizing on one representation across all write paths (either always ISO strings or always `Date`) and updating any remaining paths accordingly.

The plugin has a `logger` available from `context`, but it isn’t passed into `InMemoryDriver`, so the driver will create its own default logger and logs may not integrate with the host runtime’s logging/configuration. Consider instantiating the driver with `{ ...config, logger }` (or otherwise wiring `context.logger` into the driver).

`InMemoryDriverConfig` is described as aligned with `@objectstack/spec`’s `MemoryConfigSchema`, but it currently only models `initialData`/`strictMode`/`logger` and omits schema fields like `persistence`, `indexes`, and `maxRecordsPerObject`. This makes the type contract misleading and can hide unsupported config at compile time; either add the missing fields (even if not yet implemented) or adjust the alignment claim/docs to match what the plugin actually supports.
